# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 76 (Bi-Vb Pc76)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc76

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 76* (titled *Khiyyanadhamma* in the Pali Pātimokkha) governs the conduct of Buddhist nuns regarding communal decisions on ordination. The rule establishes that a nun commits an offense requiring confession if she initially agrees upon being refused permission by the community to give ordination, but subsequently criticizes that decision. In her analysis of the nun's disciplinary code, Ute Hüsken notes that this legal action constitutes a formal transaction with one resolution (*ñattidutiyakamma*) regarding the authorization or refusal to take on a trainee (*vuttāpanasammuti*) [Hüsken 1997]. A refusal of this authorization must be accepted unconditionally, in accordance with the regulatory principle that a nun should only be responsible for one trainee (*sikkhamānā*) at a time, and monastic members are not permitted to question a validly executed formal act of the Saṅgha [Hüsken 1997].

 Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
